newsitem.title: GERMANY: German aluminium sector sees higher 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: German aluminium sector sees higher 1997 sales.

text.p: German aluminium industry association GDA said 1997 sales should be higher than broadly steady volumes in 1996, with the exception of extrusion sales to the ailing building industry.

"We are optimistic for transport applications such as cars, trains and aircraft and also for packaging and machine building," GDA general secretary Christian Wellner told a news conference on Tuesday.
He said he believed output of rolled products and castings could rise by "three to four percent" each over 1996 volumes.
GDA put the industry's total sales values in 1996 at 21 billion marks, barely changed from 1995 -- based on evidence of recovery in the second half of the year after a weak start.

It estimated the 1996 output of aluminium semis, which include extrusions and rolled products, would be steady compared with 1.54 million tonnes in 1995, after a 3.4 percent fall in the first half of the year.
Weak building industry demand would offset a general economic recovery, which would absorb more rolled products.
GDA also said aluminium castings output in 1996 would easily match 1995's 474,000 tonnes, based on recovery prospects in the automotive industry.
GDA maintained forecasts of rising aluminium use in the key auto sector but expected tough competition with steelmakers who were also coming up with "surprising" new applications.
GDA estimates European aluminium use in cars may rise to 120 kilos per car over the next six years, from presently 65 kg in Europe and compared with presently 75-80 kg in the U.S.
Wellner added that new orders in the foil, tube, can and metal powder sectors further downstream had also picked up in recent months after a sluggish start to the year.

GDA president Walter Hueck said companies' profits would remain unsatisfactory this year despite steady sales and processors' margins were especially bad in extrusions, more than 50 percent of which are supplied to the building industry.
Some 30 percent of GDA-monitored aluminium products go into transport, followed by construction (16 percent), machine building (12) and iron and steel (10), among others.
GDA represents 102 primary and secondary producers and processors. -Vera Eckert, Duesseldorf newsroom, +49-211-3882-243
